title: Runtime Sandboxing Experiment Lab Manual
author: Maya Alvarez
body:
Overview

This manual describes the lab-grade sandboxing environment used by the runtime team to run invasive performance experiments, kernel-scheduler patches, and mixed-workload benchmarks without risking production stability. It documents the sandbox architecture, isolation model, step-by-step experiment runbook, profiling and telemetry requirements, benchmark invocation patterns, known issues encountered during experiments, and incident runbooks specific to lab activities.

Goals

- Create a reproducible, auditable environment for risky runtime changes.
- Ensure experiments are isolated from production control planes and do not leak telemetry or credentials.
- Provide a standard profiling and benchmarking workflow so results are comparable across runs.
- Capture failure modes and required mitigation steps.

Audience

- Runtime engineers doing kernel and scheduler work.
- Performance engineers running comparative benchmarks.
- SREs supporting lab infrastructure.

High-level sandbox architecture

Components

- lab-gateway: Lightweight ingress that routes experiment traffic and enforces quotas.
- kernel-orchestrator: Service that deploys custom kernel/kernelspecs into lab nodes.
- sandbox-runner: Per-node agent that configures cgroups, MIG partitions and GPU modes, and applies kernel module overrides.
- kvcache-sim: A synthetic KV cache used to emulate prefix / session caching behavior.
- telemetry-proxy: Collects and stamps telemetry for lab runs, marks data with lab_run_id, and writes to the lab telemetry bucket.

Isolation model

- Network: Lab runs live in the lab VPC (vpc-lab-1). No cross-VPC peering with prod. All egress is via nat-lab with explicit allow lists.
- Compute: Nodes are labeled "lab:true" and exist in a separate autoscaling group. Node OS images include the debug kernel and a signed kernel module whitelist.
- GPU: Two isolation modes supported: NVIDIA MPS per-experiment (for multi-process concurrency experiments) and MIG partitions (for perf isolation). sandbox-runner toggles these per experiment.
- Storage and secrets: Lab runs use ephemeral PVCs. Secrets are provided by the lab KMS with a short TTL and are not replicated to production KMS.

Kernel-scheduling considerations for lab experiments

- Scheduler variants: The lab supports several scheduler builds under kernel-orchestrator: baseline, preemptive-slice, adaptive-slice, and priority-decoupled. Each build is tagged and has a known compatibility matrix for driver and CUDA versions.
- Mapping priorities to runtime classes: Use the experiment configuration to map Redwood priority classes to kernel priorities. For example: "interactive" -> SCHED_RR with 10ms quantum; "batch" -> SCHED_DEADLINE with ED=50ms/1s.
- Fairness accounting: When testing cooperative preemption, enable kernel credit accounting (lab flag: enable_credit_accounting=true) to observe queue-smear effects.

Experiment environment provisioning

1) Request sandbox allocation

- Open RFC in the experiments tracker with: title, hypothesis, required node types, GPU mode, expected run time, and roll-back criteria. Example: "RFC: preemptive-slice latency reduction vs baseline".
- On approval, run the allocation script: ./scripts/request-lab --project runtime --nodes 4 --gputype a100 --duration 8h --labels preemptive-test

2) Provisioning checklist (automated but must be validated)

- Confirm nodes in ASG have label lab:true.
- Confirm kernel-orchestrator has deployed the requested kernel tag.
- Verify sandbox-runner applied requested GPU mode: kubectl get nodes -l lab=true -o json | jq '.items[].metadata.annotations.gpu_mode'
- Ensure telemetry-proxy is configured with lab_run_id and bucket path.

Step-by-step experiment runbook

1. Prepare experiment config (YAML)

- Minimal example (save as experiment-config.yaml):

experiment_name: preemptive-slice-compare-2026
environment: staging-sim
node_selectors:
  - lab:true
kernel_tag: preemptive-slice-v3
gpu_mode: MIG-1g.5gb
workload_profiles:
  - name: interactive
    qps: 120
    seq_length_p95: 320
  - name: batch
    qps: 2
    seq_length_p95: 2048
measurement_windows_s: 300
telemetry_bucket: s3://lab-telemetry/runtime/2026/experiment-123

2. Start with a short smoke run (10 min)

- Validate functional correctness, all services respond, and telemetry tags are present.
- Commands: ./lab-runner start --config experiment-config.yaml --smoke

3. Full run

- Start bench: ./lab-runner start --config experiment-config.yaml --duration 3600 --trace-sampling 0.1
- Monitor: kubectl top nodes -l lab=true; ./observability/quick-check --run-id=experiment-123

4. Collect artifacts

- Kernel traces: /var/log/lab/experiments/experiment-123/kernel-trace.tar.gz
- Flamegraphs: s3://lab-telemetry/runtime/2026/experiment-123/flamegraphs/
- Perf counters (per-node): s3://lab-telemetry/runtime/2026/experiment-123/perf/
- Telemetry manifest: s3://lab-telemetry/runtime/2026/experiment-123/manifest.json

Profiling playbook (lab-specific)

- Sampling strategy: Start with probabilistic sampling at 10% for p50/p95 slices and 100% sampling for all p99+ traces during the first 5 minutes and then drop to 1% for the remainder. This accelerates root-cause collection without overloading telemetry.
- Metrics to capture: per-request wall_time, kernel_queue_time, kv_cache_hit, gpu_busy_time, gpu_memory_alloc, context_switches/sec, scheduler_runqueue_length.
- Tracing hooks: Ensure runtime-gateway and kernel-orchestrator include lab_run_id and experiment_name in trace root spans.
- Perf tooling: Use perf + Nsight CLI for A100 profiling. Example: sudo perf record -a -g -- sleep 300; perf script | ./FlameGraph/stackcollapse-perf.pl | ./FlameGraph/flamegraph.pl > flame.svg

Benchmarking suite invocation

- Use the canonical runner that wraps the microbenchmark harness.
- Example command: ./bench-suite/run --profile latency --shards 4 --concurrency 64 --model redwood-v0.9-quant --seed 42 --out s3://lab-telemetry/runtime/2026/experiment-123/bench

- Config table (CSV-like text)

config_key,description,default,lab_override
shards,number of client shards,4,4
concurrency,total outstanding requests per shard,32,64
sequence_distribution,which lengths to sample,prod-like,tail-enhanced
model_variant,model binary to run,baseline,preemptive-slice-v3

Data hygiene and retention

- All lab telemetry must be tagged with lab_run_id and have a retention of 90 days by default. If an experiment is deemed sensitive, adjust confidentiality to 'restricted' and contact security.
- Do not import lab telemetry into production dashboards. To compare to production, export aggregated metrics only (no traces, no raw kernel profiles).

Release notes for this manual (v1.2)

- 2026-01-12: v1.0 initial release documenting the sandbox architecture and minimal runbook.
- 2026-01-25: v1.1 added kernel scheduling mappings and new perf counter list.
- 2026-02-03: v1.2 added MIG / MPS guidance and bench-suite invocation examples.

Known issues and mitigations (lab-specific)

- GPU driver mismatch causing node panic: Always pin driver version to node image and verify with ./scripts/verify-driver.sh. Mitigation: cordon and reprovision node with driver-consistent AMI.
- Telemetry proxy dropping spans at >2k RPS: Reduce trace sampling or scale telemetry-proxy (HPA target cpu 70%).
- kvcache-sim inconsistent TTL behavior under heavy load: Increase kvcache-sim replica_count to at least 3 and enable read-through logging.

Incident runbooks for lab activities

1) Node panic during experiment

- Step 1: Pause experiment: ./lab-runner pause --run-id=experiment-123
- Step 2: Cordon node: kubectl cordon <node-id> && kubectl describe node <node-id> | tee /tmp/node-diagnostics.txt
- Step 3: Capture kernel oops: sudo journalctl -k -b -1 > /tmp/kernel-oops.txt; attach to incident.
- Step 4: Reprovision using: ./scripts/reprovision-node --node <node-id> --ami ami-lab-debug-20260101

2) Telemetry corruption detected

- Verify manifest integrity: aws s3 cp s3://lab-telemetry/.../manifest.json - | jq .status
- If manifest shows missing files, escalate to telemetry team (owner: telemetry-eng@redwood.com) and mark run as partial.

Safety and approvals

- Any experiment that modifies kernel scheduling semantics that could change tenant isolation must have a security review and an SRE sign-off. Use the experiment-approval workflow in the tracker and attach the signed checklist.

Ownership and contacts

- Primary owner: runtime-experiments@redwood.com (team: Runtime Performance)
- On-call for lab infra: eng-sre-oncall@redwood.com (pager duty)
- Telemetry owner: telemetry-eng@redwood.com

Appendix: quick reference commands

- Request nodes: ./scripts/request-lab --nodes 4 --duration 8h
- Start bench: ./bench-suite/run --profile latency --out <s3path>
- Smoke run: ./lab-runner start --config experiment-config.yaml --smoke
- Collect kernel trace: sudo tar czf /var/log/lab/experiments/<run>/kernel-trace.tar.gz /sys/kernel/debug/tracing
